title: Bushkill Falls, Pennsylvania
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Bushkill Falls, Pennsylvania
excerpt: A charter bus to Bushkill Falls suits school and senior groups alike. The four trails, which one your group can manage, and how to plan the Poconos day.

heroImage.alt: The main hundred-foot waterfall at Bushkill Falls dropping into a wooded gorge

extraImage.alt: Wooden stairs and a footbridge crossing a stream below a waterfall at Bushkill Falls

body.text: Eight waterfalls linked by a network of wooden stairs and bridges through a Pocono gorge, the largest of them dropping about a hundred feet. Bushkill Falls has been calling itself the Niagara of Pennsylvania since long before anyone thought to check, and it remains one of the most reliable group days in the state. A charter bus to Bushkill Falls handles the one thing the site is not built for, which is fifty people arriving in fifteen cars.
It is a private attraction, not a state park

This surprises people. Bushkill Falls is privately owned, there is an admission charge, and it operates on a season — typically opening around April and closing in late autumn. Confirm both the dates and the group rate before you book a vehicle. Group pricing is available and worth asking for; it is not applied automatically.
Choose the trail before you go, not at the gate

This is the single most useful piece of planning for a group. There are four colour-coded routes of very different difficulty, and letting a mixed group decide at the ticket booth is how half of them end up somewhere they cannot manage.

items: Green trail: about fifteen minutes to the Main Falls and back. Some steps, but the shortest and most manageable option, and the right default for a senior group.
Yellow trail: around forty-five minutes, taking in the Main Falls and Lower Gorge. A good middle choice.
Blue trail: roughly an hour and a quarter, adding Bridal Veil Falls and Bridesmaid Falls.
Red trail: the full circuit at around two hours and all eight waterfalls, with a great many stairs. Fit walkers only.

body.text: Every route involves wooden stairways and boardwalks, and none of them is wheelchair accessible. Anyone in your group who cannot manage stairs should plan on the grounds, the gift shop and the small museums rather than the trails.
Which charter bus suits a Bushkill Falls group

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) is the standard vehicle for school and church groups coming from Philadelphia, New York or New Jersey, and there is room for coaches on site.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) suits a senior excursion or a smaller class and manoeuvres more easily on the Pocono back roads.
Twenty-eight to sixty: a [school bus](/fleet/school-buses) remains the most economical option for a local school district trip under two hours each way.

Getting there, and what else to build in

Bushkill sits in the Poconos near the Delaware Water Gap, about ninety minutes from Newark, two hours from Philadelphia and around two and a half from New York City. We run pickups from [East Stroudsburg](/locations/pennsylvania/east-stroudsburg), [Stroudsburg](/locations/pennsylvania/stroudsburg), [Allentown](/locations/pennsylvania/allentown) and [Philadelphia](/locations/pennsylvania/philadelphia).

The falls themselves are a half-day at most, which leaves room for the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area a few minutes south or one of the Pocono resorts. Groups searching for charter bus rental near me for a Poconos day should ask for the vehicle to stay with the group rather than booking two transfers — the region is spread out and a waiting coach turns a single stop into a proper day.
What else is on the site

The falls are the reason to come, but a group that finishes the green trail in twenty minutes needs somewhere to go. The site includes a small Native American exhibit, a wildlife museum, a maze, paddle boats on the pond, and a fudge and gift shop that reliably absorbs half an hour of any school group's day.

Practically, this means you can send fit walkers on the red trail for two hours while everybody else stays near the entrance, and the group still reassembles comfortably. That flexibility is why the site works so well for mixed-age parties — a family reunion with grandparents and eight-year-olds can genuinely all have a good day here, which is not true of most waterfall destinations.

There is a picnic area if you would rather bring lunch than buy it, which is worth knowing for a school budget. Confirm with the site whether your group can use it, as arrangements vary through the season.

Late April and May bring the highest water, when the falls are at their most impressive and the crowds have not arrived. October is the busiest and most beautiful, with the gorge in full autumn colour — book well ahead for weekends. Midsummer is pleasant and green but the flow drops noticeably in a dry August, which is worth managing expectations about.
